bull.t: Strong payment volume growth and merchant expansion
bull.b: Rapid TPV growth combined with exceptionally high customer retention indicates strong merchant adoption and increasing wallet share. This supports durable revenue expansion as existing customers scale and new payment flows are added across emerging markets.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and strong capital efficiency
bull.b: Minimal leverage limits financial risk and preserves flexibility to invest in technology, market expansion, and product development. Strong ROE also indicates that dLocal is generating substantial returns from its capital base without relying heavily on debt.

bull.t: Improving operating leverage and raised growth outlook
bull.b: Higher guidance and a rising operating-profit contribution suggest that scale, automation, and disciplined execution can convert payment growth into stronger earnings. Expected AI and automation benefits may further improve cost efficiency beyond the next two quarters.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins indicates that growth has become less profitable than in earlier periods. If mix, pricing, or processing costs remain unfavorable, future revenue gains may produce weaker earnings growth and limit operating leverage.

bear.t: Take-rate pressure from changing payment mix
bear.b: Lower take rates can structurally reduce revenue earned per dollar of payment volume, even when TPV expands rapidly. Continued growth in lower-priced corridors or larger customer discounts could therefore constrain gross-profit conversion and pricing power.

bear.t: Cash-flow consistency and regional profitability volatility
bear.b: The rebound in cash generation is encouraging, but the prior cash-flow reversal shows exposure to working-capital timing and transaction conditions. Regional spread volatility also makes earnings quality less predictable across markets and payment corridors.
